newsitem.title: ITALY: Australia urges no new U.S.-EU wheat subsidy war.
newsitem.headline: Australia urges no new U.S.-EU wheat subsidy war.

text.p: An Australian cabinet minister on Thursday attacked wheat export subsidies recently restored by the European Union and urged both Brussels and the United States not to embark on a new subsidy war.
"Our position is that we deeply regret the reintroduction of EU grain subsidies," Primary Industries and Energy Minister John Anderson told a news conference.
Anderson added that he hoped "good will on both sides" would prevail.

Anderson made his appeal as the top U.S. and EU farm officials, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, prepared to meet on the margins of a U.N. food summit to thrash out differences over grain subsidies and a range of other issues.
The two were due to meet for dinner at an undisclosed location.
Anderson said he welcomed Glickman's decision so far to hold back from restoring Washington's own subsidy programmes.
Glickman said on Wednesday he had not ruled out such a move but nothing had been finally decided.
The EU reintroduced wheat export subsidies in September after a year-long bull run in wheat prices collapsed, driving world prices to their usual position below European levels.
European and U.S. grain traders have accused Australia and especially Argentina of driving world prices lower through aggressive selling in the past weeks.
Australia says it does not act to distort markets.
